A full 3D computational study was carried out using a finite-volume based solver.
The pin/channel height used was 0.4 mm, and the pin diameters varied from 0.17-0.50 mm.
This gave hydraulic diameters in the range of 0.13-0.78 mm and volumetric area densities of 5-15 mm2/mm3.
Various heat exchanger configurations were simulated to determine performance characteristics.
Nusselt number, friction factor, specific fluid friction power, and Mach number were analyzed in the laminar flow regime.
The numerical model was validated through grid independence studies, theoretical validations, and comparisons with experimental data.
The pin surfaces generally had 50-200% higher heat transfer coefficients than the end walls.
Achieving small increases in heat transfer required disproportionate increases in friction power losses.
Nusselt number increased with increasing Reynolds number for the different configurations.
Friction factor decreased with increasing Reynolds number.
Maximum Mach number increased with Reynolds number but remained below 0.3 for the laminar conditions.
Using a slug velocity profile resulted in higher Nusselt numbers but also higher friction factors.
Key challenges include high area densities, managing pressure drops and compressibility, and accurately capturing micro-scale behavior.
The results can be useful for designing micro heat exchangers for applications like turbine blades and microelectronics.
The study provides detailed numerical diagnosis of local behavior on pin surfaces, end walls, and flow characteristics.
